trust_decision.summary: read_file with isUrl:true passes the caller-supplied URL straight to cross-fetch with no scheme, host or redirect restriction, so the MCP server can be steered to request loopback/private/link-local addresses; the decision is the missing URL trust check at the single fetch in readFileFromUrl.

landing_point.why: The summary names read_file URL fetching as the vulnerable feature, and the only fetch of a caller-supplied URL in the tree is the cross-fetch call inside readFileFromUrl, which the advisory's fix wraps with a validator.

fix_sites.module_kind: mcp tool implementation (src/tools/filesystem.ts), new private helper validateFetchUrl
mcp tool implementation, guard call at the top of the exported URL fetch function
mcp tool implementation, fetch option redirect:'error' plus redirect-aware error message (fix.diff:110-118)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The PDF branch only runs after readFileFromUrl has already fetched and validated the same URL string, so the second fetch in loadPdfToBuffer can be left alone - a solver can point at src/tools/filesystem.ts:344-346 as proof the entry check already covers it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Local PDF reading (read_file without isUrl) goes through the same parsePdfToMarkdown -> loadPdfToBuffer helper, which branches on an http(s) prefix and otherwise does fs.readFile; a guard added at that shared helper (e.g. rejecting non-http sources, or throwing for anything that is not a URL) breaks ordinary local PDF reads and the project's own parsePdfToMarkdown tests.

O6_input_shapes: URL scheme variants: file:, ftp:, gopher:, data: (only http:/https: allowed)
IPv6 literal hostnames: ::1, ::, 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1, including bracketed form
internal hostnames: localhost, host.docker.internal, metadata.google.internal, metadata.goog
dotted-decimal IPv4 in loopback 127/8, private 10/8, 172.16-31, 192.168/16, link-local 169.254/16 and 0/8
HTTP 3xx responses (handled as an error instead of being followed)
unparseable / non-absolute URL strings (new URL throws -> 'Invalid URL')

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second fetch of the same caller URL in the PDF download helper, without the scheme/host check and without redirect:'error'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists: the PDF branch of readFileFromUrl hands the raw url to parsePdfToMarkdown, and loadPdfToBuffer is an exported-code path that a maintainer would plausibly guard separately for direct callers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fetch of a configurable flag URL (DC_FLAG_URL / env default at src/utils/feature-flags.ts:30) with no host restriction
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same primitive (bare fetch of an operator-supplied URL) in a config loader; a maintainer hardening 'all outbound fetches' would route it through the same validator.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fetch of `${baseServerUrl}/api/mcp-info` where baseServerUrl comes from device config
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Another bare fetch whose base URL is configuration, so a maintainer could reasonably apply the URL guard here too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: read_multiple_files taking URLs per path (isUrl per entry) and funnelling them into readFileFromUrl
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The batch variant of read_file already exists and only lacks a per-path isUrl flag; extending URL support to it is a natural next feature that would need the same guard.

O9_family: server-side request forgery (CWE-918): unvalidated URL passed to outbound HTTP fetch

O10_build.toolchain: npm install (node_modules absent in the pinned tree) then `npm run build` = tsc + shx copies + scripts/build-ui-runtime.cjs (esbuild); `npm test` = build + node test/run-all-tests.js
O10_build.project_tests: Plain-node scripts under test/ driven by test/run-all-tests.js. test/test-file-handlers.js:19-21 exercises readFile/handleReadFile, test/test-pdf-parsing.js:8 imports parsePdfToMarkdown and test/test-pdf-parsing.js:26 fetches an external sample PDF. No test at the pinned commit covers readFileFromUrl, isUrl fetching or any URL allow/deny logic.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: String-block localhost / 127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 inside readFileFromUrl and stop, leaving redirect following and the PDF branch's second fetch untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: src/remote-device/device-authenticator.ts:69,124 and src/remote-device/device.ts:245 fetch fixed/configured service URLs for device pairing; they are outside this advisory's read_file protection and were not pursued.
The published fix itself is bypassable by hostname forms the dotted-decimal/hostname checks miss (e.g. a trailing-dot 'localhost.' or '::ffff:169.254.169.254'); recorded only as context, not pursued.
unverified: Repo size in MB: not measurable without a shell; src/ is roughly 95 TypeScript files plus a bundled pdf2md lib, so tiny_repo (<5 MB) is plausible but unconfirmed, and the flag was not raised.

markdown.ts:189 is reached only after validateFetchUrl in the same call (src/tools/filesystem.ts:344-346 runs after the guarded fetch at :327), so O2 is a real second implementation but not independently exploitable at the pinned commit; O8 is therefore empty and single_site was not raised only because O2 exists.
The published fix is effectively one function region (one new helper + two lines in readFileFromUrl); no test files are added by the diff, so regression_tests_in_pinned_commit does not apply.

Positive-path testing (an allowed public URL) needs a network peer or an /etc/hosts entry, since the guard rejects localhost/127.0.0.1; the deny logic itself is pure and testable offline. test/test-pdf-parsing.js:26 itself depends on the internet.

redirect:'error' and the redirect error branch were not verified against cross-fetch's node-fetch backend behaviour (redirection errors surface as FetchError, not the TypeError the diff checks for); behaviour of the fixed code was not run.

Whether validatePath (src/tools/filesystem.ts:219-301) can ever accept an http(s) string: it resolves the path against cwd and checks the allowed-directory list, so read_multiple_files (src/handlers/filesystem-handlers.ts:204 -> src/tools/filesystem.ts:627-632) cannot fetch URLs; inferred from reading, not run.
